notes.front: What is a system life cycle?
notes.back: The evolution of a system from conception through retirement.
notes.explanation: SP 800-160 uses the same definition of a life cycle for products, services and projects as well as systems.
notes.example: Like a car's life from the first design sketches, through years on the road, to the scrapyard.
notes.evidence: life cycle Evolution of a system, product, service, project, or other human-made entity from conception through retirement.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, Glossary, PDF p. 70

notes.front: Into which four groups does SP 800-160 sort the activities of the system life cycle?
notes.back: Technical processes, technical management processes, organisational project-enabling processes and agreement processes.
notes.explanation: Each group has its own appendix in SP 800-160, with the technical processes in Appendix H.
notes.evidence: The activities performed during the system life cycle are grouped into Technical Processes (Appendix H), Technical Management Processes (Appendix I), Organizational Project-Enabling Processes (Appendix J), and Agreement Processes (Appendix K)
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, G.1 Process Overview, PDF p. 126

notes.front: How many technical processes does SP 800-160 list, starting with Business or Mission Analysis?
notes.back: Fourteen, ending with Disposal.
notes.explanation: The later ones run Implementation, Integration, Verification, Transition, Validation, Operation, Maintenance and Disposal.
notes.evidence: System Analysis (SA) - Implementation (IP) - Integration (IN) - Verification (VE) - Transition (TR) - Validation (VA) - Operation (OP) - Maintenance (MA) - Disposal (DS)
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, Table 5 System Life Cycle Processes, PDF p. 126

notes.front: What is the security purpose of SP 800-160's Business or Mission Analysis process?
notes.back: To define the security aspects of the strategic problems or opportunities, and identify security objectives, concerns and constraints for possible solutions.
notes.explanation: It works on the problem and the potential classes of solution, not yet on a chosen design.
notes.evidence: Define the security aspects related to the strategic problems or opportunities. - Identify the security objectives, concerns, and constraints that inform the potential solution class(es).
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.1.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 131

notes.front: What is the security purpose of the Stakeholder Needs and Requirements Definition process?
notes.back: To identify the protection needs tied to the stakeholder needs and requirements for a system in a defined environment.
notes.explanation: The protection needs concern the capabilities that users and other stakeholders need from the system.
notes.evidence: Identify the protection needs associated with the stakeholder needs and requirements for a system that can protect the capabilities needed by users and other stakeholders in a defined environment.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.2.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 133

notes.front: What are two security outcomes of the Stakeholder Needs and Requirements Definition process?
notes.back: Any two of: security-relevant stakeholders identified; their security concerns identified; stakeholder assets identified; asset protection priorities determined.
notes.explanation: The outcomes move from identifying the stakeholders and their assets to setting priorities for protecting those assets.
notes.evidence: Security-relevant stakeholders of the system are identified. - Security concerns of stakeholders are identified. - Required characteristics and context for the secure use of capabilities for system life cycle concepts in system life cycle stages are defined. - Stakeholder assets and asset classes are identified. - Adversities presented by the environment are characterized. - Asset protection priorities are determined.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.2.2 Security Outcomes, PDF p. 133

notes.front: When managing stakeholder needs and requirements, SP 800-160 has the team maintain {{c1::traceability}} between stakeholder protection needs and stakeholder requirements.
notes.explanation: The same activity obtains explicit agreement that the stakeholder requirements satisfactorily address protection needs, and records asset protection data.
notes.evidence: Obtain explicit agreement that the stakeholder requirements satisfactorily address protection needs. SN-6.2 Record asset protection data. SN-6.3 Maintain traceability between stakeholder protection needs and stakeholder requirements.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.2.3 Security Activities and Tasks, PDF p. 136

notes.front: What is the security purpose of the System Requirements Definition process?
notes.back: To represent the stakeholder protection needs accurately and completely in the system requirements.
notes.explanation: It takes protection needs already expressed in the stakeholder requirements and carries them into the system requirements.
notes.evidence: Provide an accurate and complete representation of stakeholder protection needs (as expressed in the stakeholder requirements) in the system requirements.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.3.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 136

notes.front: Besides security-relevant system requirements, what else does System Requirements Definition define?
notes.back: Security-driven design constraints and security performance measures, as well as the security aspects of the system description.
notes.explanation: The system description's security aspects include its interfaces, functions and boundaries.
notes.evidence: Security aspects of the system description – including system interfaces, functions, and boundaries for a system solution – are defined. - Security-relevant system requirements and security-driven design constraints are defined. - Security performance measures are defined.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.3.2 Security Outcomes, PDF p. 136

notes.front: What is the security purpose of the System Architecture Definition process?
notes.back: To generate architecture alternatives for the protection capability, express them in consistent views and models, and support choosing one or more.
notes.explanation: The alternatives must frame stakeholder protection concerns and meet the system requirements.
notes.evidence: Generate the architectural concepts and properties of system architecture alternatives for the system protection capability that frame stakeholder protection concerns and meet system requirements. - Express the architectural concepts and properties in a set of consistent views and models. - Provide the security aspects used to select one or more architecture alternatives.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.4.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 139

notes.front: What is the security purpose of the Design Definition process?
notes.back: To provide enough detailed data and information about the security aspects of the system and its elements to realise a trustworthy secure solution.
notes.explanation: Its output is detail about security aspects, sufficient for the solution to be built.
notes.evidence: Provide sufficient detailed data and information about the security aspects of the system and its elements to realize a trustworthy secure solution
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.5.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 141

notes.front: What does SP 800-160's System Analysis process produce, from a security view?
notes.back: A rigorous basis of data and information on security aspects, to aid decision-making and technical assessments.
notes.explanation: Its analysis supports decisions and assessments across the whole life cycle, not at one point only.
notes.evidence: Produce a rigorous basis of data and information for the technical understanding of security aspects to aid decision-making and technical assessments across the life cycle.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.6.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 143

notes.front: What is the security purpose of the Implementation process?
notes.back: To transform security requirements, architecture and design into actions that create a trustworthy secure system element.
notes.explanation: The work follows the practices of the implementation technology that was selected.
notes.evidence: Transform system security requirements, architecture, and design (including interfaces) into actions that create a trustworthy secure system element according to the practices of the selected implementation technology
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.7.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 145

notes.front: One security outcome of Implementation is that system elements are securely {{c1::packaged and stored}}.
notes.explanation: The outcome beside it is that a trustworthy secure system element is realised.
notes.evidence: A trustworthy secure system element is realized. - System elements are securely packaged and stored.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.7.2 Security Outcomes, PDF p. 145

notes.front: What is the security purpose of the Integration process?
notes.back: To synthesise a set of system elements into a realised trustworthy secure system that satisfies the system requirements.
notes.explanation: It is where separately realised elements come together as one system that must meet the system requirements.
notes.evidence: Synthesize a set of system elements into a realized trustworthy secure system that satisfies the system requirements.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.8.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 147

notes.front: What is the security purpose of SP 800-160's Verification process?
notes.back: To provide objective evidence that a system, system element or artifact fulfils its specified security requirements.
notes.explanation: The artifact checked can be a document, such as the system requirements, architecture description or design description, not only a built part.
notes.evidence: Provide objective evidence that a system, system element, or artifact (e.g., system requirements, architecture description, or design description) fulfills its specified security requirements
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.9.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 149

notes.front: What is the security purpose of SP 800-160's Validation process?
notes.back: To provide objective evidence that the system, when in use, fulfils the protection needs of its mission objectives and stakeholder requirements.
notes.explanation: The test is the system's intended use in its intended operational environment, in a trustworthy secure manner.
notes.evidence: Provide objective evidence that the system, when in use, fulfills the protection needs associated with its business or mission objectives and the stakeholder requirements, thereby achieving its intended use in its intended operational environment in a trustworthy secure manner.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.11.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 154

notes.front: What is the security purpose of the Transition process?
notes.back: To preserve the system's verified security characteristics during its orderly, planned move into the intended operating environment.
notes.explanation: The intended environment may be a new one or a changed one.
notes.evidence: Preserve the system’s verified security characteristics during the orderly and planned transition of the system to be operable in the intended environment, which may be a new or changed environment.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.10.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 151

notes.front: What are two items that the security aspects of a transition strategy include, according to SP 800-160?
notes.back: Any two of: contingency back-out plans, secure shipping and receiving, security training, secure operational readiness reviews.
notes.explanation: The list is open: the strategy also covers security roles and responsibilities and facility security considerations, among others.
notes.evidence: The strategy also includes security roles and responsibilities, facility security considerations, secure shipping and receiving, contingency back out plans, security training, security aspects of installation acceptance demonstration tasks, secure operational readiness reviews
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.10.3 Security Activities and Tasks, PDF p. 152

notes.front: When a new system replaces an old one, SP 800-160 says the Transition and {{c1::Disposal}} processes are used concurrently.
notes.explanation: Commissioning the new system is considered together with securely decommissioning the old one.
notes.evidence: System commissioning is considered along with the secure decommissioning of the old system when one exists. In this case, the Transition and Disposal processes are used concurrently.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.10.3 Security Activities and Tasks, PDF p. 152

notes.front: What are two security purposes of SP 800-160's Operation process?
notes.back: Inform the security requirements and constraints for secure operation and monitoring; identify and analyse security-relevant operational anomalies.
notes.explanation: The monitoring covers products, services and operator-system performance.
notes.evidence: Inform the security aspects of the requirements and constraints to securely operate the system and monitor the security aspects of products, services, and operator-system performance. - Identify and analyze security-relevant operational anomalies.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.12.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 156

notes.front: According to SP 800-160, what does secure sustainment in the Maintenance process include?
notes.back: All maintenance and logistics activities for packaging, handling, storing and transporting replacement system elements.
notes.explanation: Maintenance aims to securely sustain the system's capability to provide a product or service.
notes.evidence: Establish the security aspects of requirements and constraints to securely sustain the capability of the system to provide a product or service. Note: Secure sustainment includes all maintenance and logistics activities for the packaging, handling, storage, and transportation of replacement system elements.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.13.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 159

notes.front: What is the security purpose of the Disposal process?
notes.back: To securely end the existence of a system or element for a specified use, and securely preserve or destroy its data and information.
notes.explanation: Disposal covers the data as well as the system: data may be preserved or destroyed, but securely either way.
notes.evidence: Provide the aspects needed to securely end the existence of a system element or system for a specified use, and securely preserve or destroy the associated data and information.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.14.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 162

notes.front: Among the Disposal outcomes in SP 800-160, what may happen to system elements?
notes.back: They are destroyed, stored, reclaimed or recycled in line with safety and security requirements.
notes.explanation: Records of the security aspects of disposal actions and analysis are also kept available.
notes.evidence: System elements are destroyed, stored, reclaimed, or recycled in accordance with safety and security requirements. - The environment is securely returned to its original secure or an agreed-upon secure state. - Records of the security aspects of disposal actions and analysis are available.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.14.2 Security Outcomes, PDF p. 162

notes.front: After disposal, SP 800-160 expects the environment to be securely returned to {{c1::its original secure state or an agreed-upon secure state}}.
notes.explanation: It is one of the security outcomes listed for the Disposal process, beside the secure handling of the elements themselves.
notes.evidence: System elements are destroyed, stored, reclaimed, or recycled in accordance with safety and security requirements. - The environment is securely returned to its original secure or an agreed-upon secure state.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.14.2 Security Outcomes, PDF p. 162

notes.front: Before any design work, a team asks the owners of a new payroll system which assets matter most, what adversities they face and which to protect first. Which SP 800-160 technical process is this?
notes.back: D) Stakeholder Needs and Requirements Definition.
notes.choices:
A) System Requirements Definition
B) Verification
C) Implementation
D) Stakeholder Needs and Requirements Definition
notes.choicesExplained: A: that process carries protection needs, once expressed, into the system requirements. B: verification checks items against specified requirements. C: implementation realises system elements.
notes.explanation: Identifying stakeholder assets, the adversities they face and asset protection priorities are outcomes of this process.
notes.evidence: Stakeholder assets and asset classes are identified. - Adversities presented by the environment are characterized. - Asset protection priorities are determined.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.2.2 Security Outcomes, PDF p. 133

notes.front: Analysts take the agreed stakeholder protection needs and write them, completely and accurately, into the requirements the system itself must meet. Which process is this?
notes.back: A) System Requirements Definition.
notes.choices:
A) System Requirements Definition
B) Stakeholder Needs and Requirements Definition
C) Validation
notes.choicesExplained: B: that process identifies the protection needs in the first place. C: validation shows the finished system meets them in use.
notes.explanation: Representing stakeholder protection needs accurately and completely in the system requirements is this process's security purpose.
notes.evidence: Provide an accurate and complete representation of stakeholder protection needs (as expressed in the stakeholder requirements) in the system requirements.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.3.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 136

notes.front: Engineers draw up three candidate structures for a system's protection capability, describe each in consistent views and models, then pick one. Which process is this?
notes.back: C) System Architecture Definition.
notes.choices:
A) Integration
B) System Requirements Definition
C) System Architecture Definition
notes.choicesExplained: A: integration combines realised elements into a system. B: requirements definition states what the system must meet, not how it is structured.
notes.explanation: Generating alternatives, expressing them in views and models and supporting the choice among them is this process's security purpose.
notes.evidence: Express the architectural concepts and properties in a set of consistent views and models. - Provide the security aspects used to select one or more architecture alternatives.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.4.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 139

notes.front: Before handover, testers check each built component against its specified security requirements and record objective evidence of the results. Which process is this?
notes.back: B) Verification.
notes.choices:
A) Validation
B) Verification
C) Transition
notes.choicesExplained: A: validation asks whether the system in use meets stakeholder needs, not whether a component meets its specification. C: transition moves the system into its operating environment.
notes.explanation: Verification confirms, with objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled.
notes.evidence: verification Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, Glossary, PDF p. 78

notes.front: After go-live, the mission owner has staff run real work on a system in its intended environment to confirm it serves their mission securely. Which process is this?
notes.back: A) Validation.
notes.choices:
A) Validation
B) Verification
C) Integration
notes.choicesExplained: B: verification checks items against specified requirements, not intended use. C: integration assembles elements into the system.
notes.explanation: Validation shows the system, when in use, meets its mission needs and stakeholder requirements in its intended environment.
notes.evidence: Provide objective evidence that the system, when in use, fulfills the protection needs associated with its business or mission objectives and the stakeholder requirements
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.11.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 154

notes.front: An organisation retires an old records server: its data is archived, its drives are destroyed and its room is returned to an agreed secure state. Which process is this?
notes.back: B) Disposal.
notes.choices:
A) Maintenance
B) Disposal
C) Transition
notes.choicesExplained: A: maintenance sustains a system that stays in service. C: transition moves a system into service.
notes.explanation: Disposal securely ends a system's existence and securely preserves or destroys its data.
notes.evidence: Provide the aspects needed to securely end the existence of a system element or system for a specified use, and securely preserve or destroy the associated data and information.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.14.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 162

notes.front: A new system is shipped to its operating site with secure handling, installed, and given a back-out plan in case go-live fails. Which process is this?
notes.back: C) Transition.
notes.choices:
A) Maintenance
B) Integration
C) Transition
notes.choicesExplained: B: integration assembles elements into a system before it moves to its site. A: maintenance sustains a system already in service.
notes.explanation: Secure shipping and receiving and contingency back-out plans are part of the transition strategy.
notes.evidence: secure shipping and receiving, contingency back out plans, security training
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.10.3 Security Activities and Tasks, PDF p. 152

notes.front: Replacement disk units for a system in service are shipped, handled and stored under controlled conditions until needed for repairs. Which process covers this?
notes.back: A) Maintenance.
notes.choices:
A) Maintenance
B) Implementation
C) Disposal
notes.choicesExplained: B: implementation realises new system elements from the design. C: disposal ends an element's existence rather than keeping spares ready.
notes.explanation: Secure sustainment includes the logistics of packaging, handling, storing and transporting replacement elements.
notes.evidence: Secure sustainment includes all maintenance and logistics activities for the packaging, handling, storage, and transportation of replacement system elements.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.13.1 Security Purpose, PDF p. 159

notes.front: A project plan groups Implementation, Integration, Verification and Transition work together under one of SP 800-160's four process groups. Which group?
notes.back: D) Technical processes.
notes.choices:
A) Technical management processes
B) Agreement processes
C) Organisational project-enabling processes
D) Technical processes
notes.choicesExplained: A: technical management covers work such as project planning and risk management. B: agreement processes cover acquisition and supply. C: project-enabling processes cover organisation-wide matters such as life cycle model management.
notes.explanation: All four appear in SP 800-160's list of technical processes, which runs from Business or Mission Analysis to Disposal.
notes.evidence: System Analysis (SA) - Implementation (IP) - Integration (IN) - Verification (VE) - Transition (TR) - Validation (VA) - Operation (OP) - Maintenance (MA) - Disposal (DS)
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, Table 5 System Life Cycle Processes, PDF p. 126

notes.front: In SP 800-160's glossary, how does verification differ from validation?
notes.back: Verification: the system was built correctly, meeting specified requirements. Validation: the right system was built, meeting its intended use.
notes.explanation: Verification compares a system or element with required characteristics; validation looks at intended use in the intended operational environment.
notes.evidence: Note: A system is able to accomplish its intended use, goals, and objectives (i.e., meet stakeholder requirements) in the intended operational environment. The right system was built. verification Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled. [78] Note: Verification is a set of activities that compares a system or system element with the required characteristics.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, Glossary, PDF p. 78

notes.front: How do stakeholder requirements differ from system requirements in SP 800-160?
notes.back: Stakeholder requirements give the users' view of desired capabilities; system requirements turn that into a technical view of a solution.
notes.explanation: System Requirements Definition is the process that makes that transformation.
notes.evidence: The purpose of the System Requirements Definition process is to transform the stakeholder, user- oriented view of desired capabilities into a technical view of a solution that meets the operational needs of the user.
notes.source: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems, H.3 System Requirements Definition, PDF p. 136
